English: Straw Guest Hut
A simple hut of wattle and daub with a straw roof, hastily assembled for wandering wayfarers and humble pilgrims.
Wooden Guesthouse
A sturdier wooden guesthouse for travelers, offering some privacy and a communal fire for warmth and prayer.
Stone Guest Quarters
Guest quarters constructed of stone, safe from the elements and offering modest comfort to visiting clergy and pious guests.
Courtyard Guesthouse
A spacious guesthouse built around a central courtyard, suitable for larger groups of pilgrims and visiting priests.
Servants' Wing
An extension for attending servants and minor dignitaries, improving the temples hospitality and reputation among the faithful.
Enclosed Guest Hall
A grand hall, fully enclosed, for hosting important guests and gatherings, strengthening religious ties and providing spiritual security.
Furnished Guest Suites
Elegant, well-appointed suites for high-ranking clergy and learned visitors, fostering religious scholarship and influence.
Chambered Guest Rooms
Private chambers with intricate decor and study nooks, attracting visiting scholars and influential clergy to the temple.
Noble Guest Apartments
Lavish apartments reserved for nobility and archbishops, enhancing the temples prestige and its role as a center for piety and learning.
Sanctuary Guest Palace
A magnificent palace, sacred and secure, for the most honored guests. Its hospitality is legendary, and it radiates piety and religious authority across the realm.
